correctness.rationale: All 65,536 vertex subsets are exactly covered by two logically independent, exhaustive rational/integer methods. One obtains the 104 allowed strict sign transversals via all 20 signed small-support linear dependencies plus bounded integer normal witnesses and counts their overlapping down-closures. The other uses strict convex containment and the Carathéodory bound of five to enumerate all 48 minimal positive dependencies among the sixteen vertices, then counts their upward closure. Both yield identical full cardinality histograms. The proof handles empty subsets, boundaries, quantifiers, all p in [0,1], and the binomial probability normalization without extrapolation.

Emamy–Meléndez (2024), doi:10.1007/978-3-031-52969-6_9, describes cubical cut-complex classes; the classification is relevant background and possibly reconstructive prior data, but the inspected text does not report the reliability polynomial.

Dyer–Füredi–McDiarmid (1992), doi:10.1002/rsa.3240030107, investigates the expected volume threshold of random hypercube vertex hulls; only the abstract was accessible and no whole-paper noncoverage assertion is made.

An expected-volume threshold does not imply exact finite-size center-retention coefficients. A stronger direct statement would supersede this claim; none was confirmed.

value.rationale: The quantity is the exact center-retention reliability of the first small Boolean cube allowing minimal positive supports of five vertices. It is a natural coverage invariant in random 0/1-polytope models, yielding conditional cardinality-specific probabilities and the entire Bernoulli law. Its overlapping transversals require more than reading the known 104 threshold count; the 48-support dual classification gives independent geometric understanding and a reusable exact benchmark. The result is finite but canonically motivated, rather than an arbitrary parameter slice.
